title: Your body belongs to you: safe and unsafe touch
examples: What is safe touch and unsafe touch?
What do I do if someone touches me and I do not like it?
Who should I tell if a touch feels wrong?

explain.say: Here is something very important that every child should know: your body belongs to you. You are the boss of your body. Look at the board. Some touches are safe and feel good.

draw.text: Your body belongs to you: safe and unsafe touch

explain.say: Safe touches are things like a high five, a hug you want, or holding hands. A doctor or nurse might need to check you, with a parent or carer there. These touches keep you happy and healthy. Can you name another safe touch?

Now look at the unsafe group: touches that hurt you, that make you scared, or that touch your private parts, the parts covered by your swimsuit. And if someone says, keep this touch a secret, that is unsafe too.
If a touch feels wrong, remember these steps. Say no, loudly: No! Stop! Then get away to a safe place. Can you say no in a big, strong voice?

explain.say: Then tell a trusted adult straight away, like a parent, carer, teacher or grandparent, and keep telling until someone helps. It is never your fault, and you will not be in trouble. You did so well learning this.

faq.q: What is safe touch and unsafe touch?
faq.a: Safe touch, like a high five or a hug you want, feels good and keeps you safe. Unsafe touch hurts, scares you, touches your private parts, or comes with being told to keep it secret.
asks: Tell me about the Safe touch
Tell me about the Unsafe touch

faq.q: Who should I tell if someone touches me in a way I do not like?
faq.a: Tell a trusted adult straight away, like a parent, carer, teacher, grandparent or school counsellor. If they do not help, tell another one, or call a child helpline.
asks: Tell me about the Tell a trusted adult
Who should I tell if a touch feels wrong?

faq.q: Will I get in trouble for telling?
faq.a: No. You will never be in trouble for telling a trusted adult about a touch. It is never your fault, even if the person is someone you know.
asks: Tell me about the Not your fault

faq.a: Private parts are the parts of your body covered by underwear or a swimsuit. Nobody should touch them or ask to see them, except to keep you clean or healthy, like a doctor with your parent there.
asks: Tell me about the Private parts

faq.q: Can I say no to a hug from a relative?
faq.a: Yes. You can say no thank you and offer a high five or a wave instead. Your body belongs to you.
asks: Do I have to hug people?

facts: The UK children's charity NSPCC teaches the PANTS rule, which includes "Always remember your body belongs to you".
The Council of Europe's Underwear Rule teaches children that nobody should touch them where their underwear covers.
